newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity futures end up after soft open.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity futures end up after soft open.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures moved down in early trade Friday, then rallied late in the day to settle higher, traders said.
"There wasn't much going in the fundamentals, but a big buyer came in and pushed prices up," said one dealer.
Traders noted the September California-Oregon border (COB) contract saw support from continued tightness in Northwest hydropower supplies.

As of early Friday, turbines totaling 1,425 MW of power capacity were off line at the massive Grand Coulee Dam in Washington state, but one 600 MW unit at the project was scheduled to restart later in the day.
September COB rose 64 cents per megawatt hour (MWh) to settle at $22.73 after dipping to $21.70 earlier.
October COB closed 3 cents higher at $21.23 and November ended up 20 cents at $22.50.
Palo Verde electricity for September delivery gained 5 cents to settle at $28.68 per MWh, compared with a high for the day of $28.80 and a low of $28.05.
October PV closed 35 cents higher at $22.30, while November was up 10 cents at $21.90.
Separately, the 750 MW unit 5 at the Four Corners coal-fired power complex in New Mexico was expected to restart Sunday after being shut earlier this month for repairs.
The 254 MW unit 1 at the Valmy coal-fired power plant in Nevada was expected to restart Sunday or Monday after being shut earlier this week due to a rotor problem.
In the latest six to 10 day weather forecast for the Southwest, Weather Services Corp predicted near or just above normal temperatures.
In the Northwest, the forecast was for temperatures of one to five degrees F below normal with near or just above normal precipitation.
Transmission capacity on the Pacific Intertie, which links the Pacific Northwest to Southern Califoria, remained at 6,300 MW pending final approval of system operating procedures.
Once those are cleared, which is expected by Monday, the rating will be lifted to 6,900 MW.
